hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap over next 20 years
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next two decades, a gap that could shape how residents get around for years to come. The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. The county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Of the available funding, all but $10 million comes from state and federal sources.

Nine roads identified as requiring widening to handle growing traffic remain unfunded, with a total cost of approximately $213 million. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. All nine projects are left out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. May and Maddy Brumlow, who travel Martin Downs Boulevard nearly every day, said the congestion is already noticeable. "There's always traffic, it's always backed up," Maddy Brumlow said. Beth Beltran, administrator for Martin County's Metropolitan Planning Organization, said funding shortfalls of this scale are common. "I don't think I know of one MPO in the whole country where the needs are equal to the revenue," Beltran said.

State Road 710 ranks among the county's highest priorities due to repeated safety concerns. "Fatal crashes as well as serious injury crashes were just enormous out there," Beltran said. The draft plan includes several SR-710 projects that are already funded or programmed, totaling about $300 million, including a realignment at CR-714/Martin Highway and widening from CR-609 to SW Van Buren Road. The projects also include additional widening segments totaling nearly 16 miles.

The draft Cost Feasible Plan totals approximately $746 million in year-of-expenditure dollars across multiple categories. Highway and roadway projects account for $213.97 million, including SR-710 improvements and widening of Cove Road, SW Newfield Parkway, High Meadow Avenue, and a new Willoughby Boulevard Extension. Turnpike projects total $274.81 million, including a new interchange study at milepost 125, direct connect ramps, and widening north of SR-714 to north of Becker Road. Transit improvements total $160.4 million, covering fixed route and paratransit service, new microtransit zones, new fixed route service along Kanner Highway and a Jensen Beach Trolley, fleet replacement, and bus stop upgrades. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce residents pack planning meeting over 17-story Causeway Cove high-rise development
cards.body:
The Fort Pierce Planning Board reviewed the Causeway Cove development project on Monday, drawing a packed chamber of neighbors concerned about the proposal. The project, located off Seaway Drive, includes five high-rise buildings, including a 17-story building standing 192 feet tall, more than four times the city's height limit. Plans also call for two hotels and more than 70,000 square feet of retail space.

The development qualifies under the Live Local Act, a state law passed in 2023 that allows developers to bypass height and density restrictions as long as they set aside 40% of units for affordable housing for at least 30 years. The project includes more than 900 apartments and condos, with 365 of those designated as affordable housing. Residents at the meeting expressed concerns about traffic and the character of the area. Buster Brewster, a boater at Causeway Cove Marina, said he worries the project will alter the area's appeal. "We're going to put this big old conglomerate up here, and I'm just afraid it's going to take away from the beauty of this place," Brewster said. Dennis Fein raised concerns about traffic at the meeting. "Nobody's thought this out. You're going to have massive traffic jams. Nobody's going to be able to get on the island, off the island," Fein said.

City Planning Director Kev Freeman said developers must add traffic mitigation efforts and any required intersection or access improvements. City Commissioner Michael Broderick said the city has no authority over whether the project is approved. "The city does not have a play here. We do not have a position in this. This is regulated by the state of Florida in the entirety. The city has been eliminated from the process," Broderick said.

City commissioners are scheduled to hear a review of the project as the next step in the process.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie residents oppose commercial rezoning near Tradition
cards.teaser: A proposed land use change near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive is heading to Port St. Lucie City Council for a final vote Monday after neighbors expressed concerns about how commercial development could impact their community.
cards.body:
Joseph and Margaret Mucciolo live along the edge of the nearly 9.5-acre property near Crosstown Parkway and SW Fairgreen Drive. Two months ago, they told WPTV they feared changing the land from residential to commercial could alter the character of the community they moved to call home. Joseph Mucciolo said if these things come to pass, they may seek other grounds and other places to go. The proposal is scheduled for a second reading and final vote before city council Monday.

The request, submitted by Winding River Crosstown, LLC, would amend the Tradition Master Planned Unit Development plan by removing the property from a residential designation and creating a new parcel designated for retail and office uses. The city says the change would allow for future commercial development on the site, but any future project would still need to go through additional review and approval processes. The Planning and Zoning Board recommended approval of the amendment with conditions in May. Those conditions include a 10-foot enhanced landscape buffer and architectural wall along portions of the property bordering residential areas, requirements to limit lighting impacts, and eliminating a possible future connection to SW Glenbrook Drive. Margaret Mucciolo said they do not want over development.

cards.headline: Rising home insurance costs drive 65% of Florida voters toward midterm polls, study finds
cards.body:
Homeowners insurance costs are emerging as a decisive political issue for Florida voters as the 2026 midterm elections approach, according to a new study from online insurance marketplace Insurify. The study found 65% of Florida respondents said rising insurance costs would make them more likely to vote in the 2026 midterms, compared to 58% of Americans nationally who say the same. Insurify economist Julia Taliesin said the research aimed to examine potential connections between the political environment and insurance regulation in certain states.

The study reveals substantial engagement among Florida voters on housing costs. According to the findings, 84% of Florida respondents plan to vote in the 2026 midterms, with 72% of Florida respondents identifying as homeowners. Among Florida homeowners, 49% reported their home insurance premiums increased in the last 12 months. Insurify puts the Florida statewide average premium at $8,292, with a modest 2% increase expected this year. The data also shows 57% of Florida respondents feel negative about the state of the economy, while 71% believe elections affect home insurance costs in their state.

State leaders point to insurance litigation reforms as having led to stable and in many cases lower rates, as more companies enter Florida and add to competition. However, in many parts of the state, including South Florida, insurance premiums have risen as inflation and home values have increased. The disconnect between reform efforts and actual premium costs in certain regions highlights the complexity of the insurance issue facing both voters and policymakers.

Republican state leaders this year have been leading the charge for property tax reform as a new affordability target. Taliesin suggested insurance complexity may be driving that political shift in focus. "It demonstrates about what is easiest to shift where they can focus and get maybe the biggest result, and insurance is complicated," she said. The study results indicate Florida voters are paying close attention to housing affordability issues heading into the elections, with insurance costs specifically motivating turnout decisions across the state. The data suggests homeowners insurance has become a significant factor in political engagement as residents grapple with rising costs despite legislative efforts to stabilize the market.

cards.headline: Florida Democrats claim path to breaking Republican supermajorities in state legislature
cards.teaser: Florida Democratic Party leaders outlined a strategy Monday they say could break Republican supermajorities in the state legislature, pointing to more than 30 local and special-election flips since 2024.
cards.body:
Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said Monday the Republican supermajority in the legislature is breakable this cycle. The party pointed to more than 30 local and special-election flips since the 2024 election, more than 3,000 volunteers, increased candidate recruitment and an advantage in requests for vote-by-mail ballots. The party's tally includes local offices as well as recent legislative special elections, not 30 seats in the Florida Legislature. Fried said the difference this cycle is the party's Pendulum Project, a year-round organizing operation designed to maintain voter contact between major elections. Senate Democratic Leader-designate Tracie Davis said the party has put in place programs needed to break the supermajorities. Democrats are also counting on a political pattern that has helped opposition parties in past midterm elections, believing dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump and economic conditions could help them reconnect with working-class voters, younger Floridians and voters with no party affiliation.

Democrats are building their message around affordability, blaming nearly three decades of Republican control for rising housing, property insurance, healthcare and everyday living costs. Fried said the party's candidates will also challenge a Republican-backed property tax amendment headed to voters, arguing that cutting local government revenue could threaten services or shift costs elsewhere. Republicans have promoted the measure as a way to provide relief to homeowners facing higher tax bills. Democrats argue the proposal does not address property insurance premiums and could squeeze funding for police, fire departments, roads, parks and other local services. The party will continue making its case at Leadership Blue, the state party's annual gathering scheduled for July 17 through 19 at Disney's Coronado Springs Resort in Lake Buena Vista. Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg will deliver the keynote address at the July 18 gala.

hero.headline: Pickup truck fire closes lane on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County
hero.body:
St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to a vehicle fire Monday morning on Florida's Turnpike Northbound near Mile Marker 175. Firefighters arrived to find a fully involved Ford F-250 pickup truck on the shoulder of the interstate.

Crews initiated an aggressive fire attack, bringing the fire under control while working alongside the Florida Highway Patrol to maintain a safe scene for motorists. Traffic was temporarily impacted as firefighters extinguished the fire and secured the scene.

No additional vehicles were involved in the incident. The pickup truck was completely engulfed in flames when firefighters arrived at the scene.

The cause of the fire is under investigation. Firefighters worked to secure the scene after extinguishing the blaze.

hero.headline: World Cup semifinals set with England, Argentina, France and Spain advancing
hero.teaser: England and Argentina won their quarterfinal matches over the weekend to complete the World Cup semifinal lineup. The four highest-ranked teams in the tournament will compete in the final four.
hero.body:
England beat Norway behind two goals from Jude Bellingham, while Argentina defeated Switzerland with a goal from Julián Alvarez in extra time. The 23-year-old Bellingham was described as being "everywhere on the pitch" as he inspired his team past Erling Haaland's Norway. Alvarez scored what was called an "absolute worldie" in extra time to help Argentina advance, though the match also featured a controversial VAR call. Both Bellingham and Harry Kane have scored six goals in the competition, carrying England through difficult matches. England was last in a World Cup semifinal in 2018 but lost to Croatia.

Argentina has relied on Lionel Messi and his teammates to advance, with the defending champion scoring the most goals of anyone in the competition with 17. The team has flirted with elimination on more than one occasion but knows how to win ugly when necessary. Argentina has the added advantage of experience, with many members of the current squad winning the title in 2022. Despite not being a beautiful team to watch, Argentina has found ways to produce moments of brilliance in the knockout rounds. Argentina will face England in the semifinal.

France will play Spain in the other semifinal in Dallas on Tuesday. France has been considered the tournament favorite and has advanced with ease, barely getting out of first gear according to observers. The team has relied on its ridiculously talented front line, with Kylian Mbappé proving superb with his pace and directness. He is supported by Ousmane Dembélé and other attackers who make France a frightening opponent. Legendary manager Didier Deschamps is leaving his role after this tournament, and France will be looking to replicate its 2018 success by sending him away with another World Cup winner's medal.

Spain has also reached the semifinals though it has not set the world alight with its performances. Teenage superstar Lamine Yamal has yet to really thrive, which might be related to an injury he was nursing coming into the tournament. However, the midfield and defense are looking strong, and Spain has conceded just one goal the entire tournament. Despite France being the narrow favorite, recent history favors Spain. La Roja beat France in the Euro 2024 semifinals, a tournament it went on to win, and also defeated Les Bleus in the Nations League last year. The winner of the France-Spain match will likely be favorite to win the title on July 19.

cards.headline: Jannik Sinner defeats Alexander Zverev to win second straight Wimbledon title
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7, 7-6, 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday to win his second consecutive Wimbledon championship and fifth Grand Slam title overall.
cards.body:
Top-ranked Jannik Sinner beat Alexander Zverev 6-7 (7), 7-6 (2), 6-3, 6-4 on Sunday for his fifth Grand Slam title and second consecutive Wimbledon championship. When Sinner ripped a forehand winner up the line on his first match point, the Italian dropped to the grass on his back in celebration. The victory marked Sinner's 10th straight win over Zverev, who was coming off his first Grand Slam title at the French Open. Prince William joined his wife Kate and two of their children for the final in a star-studded Royal Box that also included actors Dustin Hoffman, Nicole Kidman and Ben Stiller.

The match shifted at 3-3 in the third set when Zverev earned his first break point 2 hours and 42 minutes into the match. Sinner produced a drop shot and Zverev slipped and appeared to hyper-extend his right knee as he attempted to change directions behind the baseline. Zverev grasped his knee in apparent discomfort and Sinner went around the net and helped his opponent up off the grass. Zverev quickly resumed playing but appeared slightly hampered and slung his racket across the baseline in frustration when he missed a forehand, handing Sinner the first break of the match and a 5-3 lead in the third. The title came in Sinner's first tournament since a second-round meltdown at the French Open in late May, when he wilted in a Paris heat wave.

cards.headline: Linda Noskova wins Wimbledon women's title in all-Czech final
cards.teaser: The 21-year-old Czech player Linda Noskova recovered from wasting five match points to defeat Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy.
cards.body:
Linda Noskova recovered from a second-set meltdown in which she wasted five match points to overcome Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 in an all-Czech final on Saturday for her first Grand Slam trophy. The 21-year-old became the third Czech woman in four years to win the grass-court major, after Marketa Vondrousova in 2023 and Barbora Krejcikova in 2024.

Petra Kvitova, who won Wimbledon in 2011 and 2014, was in attendance, as was Martina Navratilova, who won a record nine singles titles at the All England Club. Navratilova looked on from the Royal Box, where she was seated next to Kate, the Princess of Wales, who was due to present the Venus Rosewater Dish trophy to Noskova. Muchova and Noskova played doubles together at the 2024 Paris Olympics and finished fourth. In the men's final on Sunday, top-ranked Jannik Sinner will attempt to defend his title against French Open champion Alexander Zverev.

cards.headline: Florida Republicans hold voter registration advantage of more than 1.5 million
cards.teaser: As of May 31, Florida had about 5.54 million active registered Republicans and 4.03 million Democrats, according to the state Division of Elections, with another 3.32 million voters registered without a party affiliation.
cards.body:
Republicans have built a voter registration advantage of more than 1.5 million in Florida. As of May 31, Florida had about 5.54 million active registered Republicans and 4.03 million Democrats, according to the state Division of Elections. Another 3.32 million voters were registered without a party affiliation. Republicans remain at or above the two-thirds threshold needed for supermajority power in both legislative chambers. A two-thirds majority amounts to 80 of the 120 House seats and 27 of the 40 Senate seats when every member is present.

Gov. Ron DeSantis defeated Democrat Charlie Crist by roughly 19 percentage points in 2022. Two years later, Trump carried Florida over Kamala Harris by about 13 points, the largest Republican presidential margin in the state since 1988. Political analyst Susan MacManus said Democrats must generate enthusiasm among supporters who have skipped recent elections while also winning a sizable share of unaffiliated voters. Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried said the party has seen an advantage in requests for vote-by-mail ballots and has more than 3,000 volunteers working through the Pendulum Project, a year-round organizing operation designed to maintain voter contact between major elections. Democratic leaders argued late in the 2024 cycle that Florida was competitive, but the promised surge did not translate into enough votes.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap over next 20 years
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next two decades, a gap that could shape how residents get around for years to come. The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. The county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Of the available funding, all but $10 million comes from state and federal sources.

Nine roads identified as requiring widening to handle growing traffic remain unfunded, with a total cost of approximately $213 million. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. All nine projects are left out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. May and Maddy Brumlow, who travel Martin Downs Boulevard nearly every day, said the congestion is already noticeable. "There's always traffic, it's always backed up," Maddy Brumlow said. Beth Beltran, administrator for Martin County's Metropolitan Planning Organization, said funding shortfalls of this scale are common. "I don't think I know of one MPO in the whole country where the needs are equal to the revenue," Beltran said.

State Road 710 ranks among the county's highest priorities due to repeated safety concerns. "Fatal crashes as well as serious injury crashes were just enormous out there," Beltran said. The draft plan includes several SR-710 projects that are already funded or programmed, totaling about $300 million, including a realignment at CR-714/Martin Highway and widening from CR-609 to SW Van Buren Road. The projects also include additional widening segments totaling nearly 16 miles.

The draft Cost Feasible Plan totals approximately $746 million in year-of-expenditure dollars across multiple categories. Highway and roadway projects account for $213.97 million, including SR-710 improvements and widening of Cove Road, SW Newfield Parkway, High Meadow Avenue, and a new Willoughby Boulevard Extension. Turnpike projects total $274.81 million, including a new interchange study at milepost 125, direct connect ramps, and widening north of SR-714 to north of Becker Road. Transit improvements total $160.4 million, covering fixed route and paratransit service, new microtransit zones, new fixed route service along Kanner Highway and a Jensen Beach Trolley, fleet replacement, and bus stop upgrades. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August.

cards.headline: Jonathan Dickinson State Park concession closed indefinitely, boat rentals and tours unavailable
cards.teaser: The concession operation at Jonathan Dickinson State Park is closed indefinitely after the vendor's contract expired, leaving visitors without access to boat rentals, canoe rentals, and the Loxahatchee Queen tour to Trapper Nelson's Island.
cards.body:
Jonathan Dickinson State Park's concession operation is closed indefinitely this summer, leaving visitors without access to boat rentals, canoe rentals, and the popular Loxahatchee Queen tour to Trapper Nelson's Island. Park officials told WPTV the vendor who operated the concession had their contract expire. The park is now searching for a new vendor, but warns the approval process is lengthy and could take months.

Max Santos, a Jupiter local who has been coming to the park his entire life, said he and others were caught off guard when they arrived to find the concession office closed. Santos said the concession previously allowed visitors to access bike rentals, canoes, motorboats and tours, and provided a place to get refreshments after activities. Daniela Sellitti drove from West Palm Beach with her kids hoping to take them on the Loxahatchee Queen to Trapper Nelson's Island, only to find the service unavailable. The park website says the concession is closed indefinitely. Sellitti said she hopes the park can find a contract with someone else who will open a concession and get the boats running again so visitors can enjoy the river and get a chance to visit Trapper Nelson's Island, which she called a part of Florida history.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

cards.headline: Pickup truck fire closes lanes on Florida's Turnpike in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded Monday morning to a fully involved Ford F-250 pickup truck fire on the shoulder of Florida's Turnpike Northbound.
cards.body: St. Lucie County Fire District crews responded to a vehicle fire Monday morning on Florida's Turnpike Northbound near Mile Marker 175 and found a fully involved Ford F-250 pickup truck on the shoulder of the interstate. Crews initiated an aggressive fire attack and brought the fire under control while working alongside the Florida Highway Patrol to maintain a safe scene for motorists. Traffic was temporarily impacted as firefighters extinguished the fire and secured the scene. No additional vehicles were involved. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

hero.headline: Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse offers 165 years of history with 105-step climb to panoramic views
hero.teaser: The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse, built in 1860, offers visitors a 105-step climb to panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean, Jupiter Inlet, and Loxahatchee and Indian rivers.
hero.body:
The Jupiter Inlet Lighthouse stands 165 years after its construction in 1860, serving as both an active navigational aid and a destination for visitors seeking to experience its history and panoramic views. The red brick tower at the base of the Jupiter Inlet on Florida's Atlantic coast has guided mariners continuously since before the Civil War while opening its doors to the public who want to climb to its observation gallery.

Reaching the top requires ascending 105 steps up a narrow spiral staircase that winds through the interior of the brick tower. This route follows the same path that lighthouse keepers climbed night after night throughout history to maintain the powerful Fresnel lens that projected light across the water to passing ships. The spiral staircase leads visitors upward through the tower to the gallery that sits at the top of the structure, retracing the steps of the early keepers who ensured the beacon remained operational.

The observation gallery at the top provides panoramic views stretching across multiple waterways and the ocean. The Atlantic Ocean extends to the east, while below the tower, the turquoise waters of the Jupiter Inlet converge with the Loxahatchee and Indian rivers. Visitors at this elevated vantage point can watch boats glide through the channel as sea breezes sweep across the observation area. The commanding perspective reveals why this location proved ideal for a lighthouse, offering clear sightlines across the coastal landscape and waterways.

The museum grounds preserve more than just the tower itself. Restored historic buildings chronicle the lighthouse's journey from its construction before the Civil War through its years as an active Coast Guard station. These structures provide information about the lighthouse's role in regional maritime history and offer details about the daily lives of the keepers who operated the station. The site maintains the supporting buildings that allowed the lighthouse station to function across more than a century and a half of continuous service, preserving the complete story of this working navigational aid that has marked the Florida coastline for generations of mariners.
